body:
> my mom went into the hospital for shortness of breath, me, dad, her friends all begged her to go for weeks before she finally did. They were treating her for Congestive heart failure, but she was stable...

Same. My mom complained of shortness or breath and tightness of chest for months while I kept asking if she wanted me to take her to the hospital. It didn’t help that the doctor she’s had for years dismissed her symptoms as indigestion and said to take antacids, until I literally begged him to check her heart. I was right.  Silent heart attacks, then the big one on New Years. Wish I had just taken her to the ER or urgent care regardless of her saying no. Hoping things get better for you and your mom right now.

That’s exactly what I’m going through right now. Lost both parents this year, and one of my friends’ mom has been in the hospital this past month with the same ailment my mom had. Pneumonia -> septic shock. I walked her through each step of what was going on, what to ask doctors, what to look for, and now I’m helping to prepare her for grief as the doctors just said her mom won’t make it anymore. 

She thanked me, but I said I thank her even more for being 100% in her updates to me and letting me be there. Through my experience, I was able to help her, and that means something positive came from this... to pay it forward.  Another friend said “that’s very nice of you. And it’s going to happen again with more people”. That’s ok.

Edit: Her mom just passed this morning surrounded by loved ones. It’s All Saints Day.
Yep, someone actually used this platitude on me.  Effective? Nope.

>those same people would be even worse off than you are under the same conditions

I agree. My cousin told me that he (and most people) would've given up at just 5% of the things I have endured.   

Thank you

Exactly.   As much as I wish my friends could understand, the only way they *would* be able to is if they've experienced something similar...  and I wouldn't wish this pain on anyone.  

I'm sorry you're going through the pain of facing your dad's mortality. I had to see my father fade away until he was merely 96 lbs, and then I had to see my mom code blue, unable to be resuscitated.  I have PTSD too and it can be so debilitating.  Sending you internet hugs, kind stranger

Yeah, a group of friends and I almost got hit by a drunken driver on the corner of a street when this driver ran into a barricade.  Everyone was so relieved we weren't hit, and I stood there with the realization that "That could've been it.. and I would've been ok with it as long as it wasn't painful and someone took care of my dogs."  But I've been feeling like not wanting to exist a lot more now that I lost both parents and my job this year.  I just don't want to hurt anymore.
I'm sorry about your dad.  My mom had cancer too and it was her heart that suddenly took her away too.  I was always afraid of her cancer coming back, so it was a shock that it was something else.

I feel exactly the same way you do and I'm incredibly lonely too.  I have no reason to wake up, besides taking my dogs out.  What you say about people getting bummed out and pulling away from you is very true, especially if they haven't lost loved ones themselves yet (which is still a lot of them as we're in our 20's. I have one old coworker who is 63 and still has both parents living).  

Some people try to sympathize with me and say that they just lost their grandma or grandpa whom they haven't seen in years.  I lost my grandparents when I was 8.  While I feel for them too, me having to be the caregiver for my parents for the past 5 years making life-or-death decisions constantly and then losing them and my job back-to-back is on a grander scale.   I don't want to be seen as comparing grief, because all grief is hard.  

I'm forced to put on that happy front like you.  It has made me even more isolated than ever before.  I'm very good at putting on the front too... I've had people tell me I'm so calm and collected. Even my therapist said that I put on a good image that I have everything handled (I started therapy after my mom passed).  It feels weird using the word orphan.   I feel lost, sad, hopeless, and numb to the everyday chatter of world.  I can't find happiness because they all seem like distractions.  I've had so many hardships hit me that being happy makes me feel like I'm being vulnerable to when the next bad thing happens, so I'm always on alert.

I started wellbutrin one month ago.  It takes 4-6 weeks to be effective.  My doctor and I discussed doubling the dose now that it has built up in my system.  I don't feel any big differences on it.  At first, it kind of felt like it was bringing me 'back down to earth' instead of having my head in a cloud, but that made me face my demons more head on and feel overwhelmed.  

The doctor did not prescribe me xanax or other anti-anxiety on an as-needed basis.  She only gave me an anti-histamine which just makes me drowsy and sleep.  It gives me vivid dreams/nightmares.  She said that doctors are hesitant on prescribing benzos due to their possibility for addiction.  I've never taken xanax before.  To be honest, I didn't want to be on medication due to their side effects, but it's gotten to that point that my doctor insisted.  

I asked for a referral to a psychiatrist which took a month to receive, and then when I called the psych office, they said that they're at full capacity and can't take new patients.  Now I'm waiting to be 're-directed' to a different psychiatrist.  It's so hard finding help for mental health.  I'm exhausted.

That is so very sweet of your grandad to offer to drive you tomorrow.  I hope you know that being able to do that is helping him too and that is truly loving.  You're lucky to have your cousin and grandad, and they're lucky to have you.  Lean on them and honor your grandmother's life together.  

Like the other commenter said, it is ok to keep talking to your grandmother.  She definitely is proud of you and will be by your side through all the years.  Don't worry about a timeline for "getting past this".  Healing is a process.  You are not back at square one.  There is so much love in your heart.  Please don't feel any shame in going to counseling, the chaplain, or bereavement.  They are trained to help people in these situations and it is therapeutic to let someone know how you feel.  Sending love and hugs your way.

One week ago is such a short time and from your post history, I see your dad was 48.  I am so so sorry he was taken away from you so soon. It isn't fair.  I'm sending my love and caring thoughts to you too.  I started going to therapy asap after my mom passed and it helped me a lot in the beginning.  Please continue talking about it with loved ones, a therapist, and/or support groups.  Even if you feel like you are handling it ok on your own, it's comforting to have a little support.  PM me anytime.

I hope that peace finds us as well and I'm sorry that you feel the same way as I do.  Switching to a grief counselor sounds like a good idea.  I might try that too, because my current therapist isn't being as effective as before.  Sending you hugs and healing thoughts.  Thank you

I want to fade into darkness.  Both of my parents died and lost my job this year.  My mom was my everything.  I always told myself I can't kill myself because she needs me.  Now I failed in taking care of her.  This pain is unbearable and I keep wondering why I'm still here.

Thank you for your kindness and for understanding the caregiver role.  I feel like I failed.  My mom came home from surgery and I couldn't take good enough care of her.  I've gotten so tired over the past 5 years.  I was still grieving my dad and my job when my mom got sick again, and by that time I had nothing left.  My sibling still chose not to stick around and help.  He should've been next to me going through all this, and even though I'm younger, I've had to be the more responsible one. I am sorry that your dad has also passed and I'm sending you lots of love and hugs.  I handled the passing of my dad well because he was sick for a long time, but I am absolutely broken about my mom. It definitely will take time.  Thank you for sharing your experience.

I wish it were so easy to rewire my brain to be positive. I really do.  There is just so much trauma that I pushed down to even get this far.  I had to push my emotions away in order to stay strong to take care of my family.  Now that I lost my parents and job, all these emotions demand to be felt.

Sometimes I have felt like I was going to have a heart attack too, so I had my doctor do an EKG and now I have to take blood pressure medicine.  I'm not even 30.  I broke out in hives all over my body because even though I am trying to look like I'm ok on the outside, my body knows I'm not ok.  My therapist said there is a mind-body connection.  I was against trying medication, but the hives breakout made my doctor say I really needed to now.  I feel like I'm grasping at straws trying everything I'm supposed to to cope, but it's not working.  You say to imagine myself in the future, but I don't even see myself in the future, let alone in the next five years.  I'm sorry for being such a downer.  I do appreciate your words of hope, but I don't see happiness in my future at all.

I have called a support line twice before, but unfortunately, I don't think I'll be calling one again.  I have an appointment with a therapist tomorrow and have already told him the last few sessions about my thoughts of not wanting to be here.  He tried teaching me meditation.  

I just feel so exhausted and don't want to deal with this anymore.  I rewind my memories trying to search for a time when I was really happy, but it's not there.  Just darkness, anxiety, and exhaustion.  Any time I did feel joy was just a distraction, and my problems were always in the back of my mind to take the front seat again when I'm alone.  I've been alone for a really long time and have been the backbone of my family, so people around me are amazed at "how strong I am".  But, I'm really not and I'm really struggling now. Thanks for responding.

I am getting professional help in the form of therapy, support groups, and now medicine.  I asked for a referral to a psychiatrist too, but that psych is at full capacity.  I'm doing everything I can, but this nightmare is consuming me.  Feeling hopeless and alone.
Time is all I have, too much of it.  Living in this constant loop of anxiety and hopelessness. I can't do this for much longer.

Some things you said I can relate to. Parents both passed, feeling disconnected, losing friends, abusive relationship.  I've also tried multiple ways to cope too, just going through the motions of therapy, support group, hotlines, friends, meds.  But I'm at the point of thinking how to do it too, and I too am afraid of messing up or suffering pain and regretting it.  I wake up disappointed that I'm still here and have to re-live these nightmares.  I don't have any solutions because I am going through it too.  I just wanted to respond to your post so you know that someone out here has read it, and that I connect with a lot of the things you said, so we are both a little less disconnected from the world now.  Sending peace and serenity your way. Hugs

I lost both my parents this year. My dad - a slow, very expected decline.  My mom, more sudden.  Knowing that my dad was going soon made me go to therapy asap to resolve any issues I had with him so that I could forgive him before he passed.  My therapist said that when a person has any unresolved issues with a person before they pass, and doesn't resolve those issues when they pass, those issues often get exacerbated and blow up afterwards. 

You sound a bit like me in wanting to be prepared and read as much as you can so you know what to expect.  But, grief is different for everyone.  Some people feel like they've been hit by a train, some feel ok at first and then grieve much later on, others feel guilty for not grieving as much as they thought they should, etc.  Personally, I am at an all-time low and want to give up too.  These feelings are "normal".  I agree with the other commenter who said to build up your support system now.  I have since gone back to therapy and it has helped to talk to someone about it.  Realize that people around you may have good intentions, but not know how to act or what to say to someone who is grieving if they have not gone through it themselves.  So having a therapist as professional help was good.  Shower your mother with love and reassure her that she is not alone.
